clauses.reason: Terminated on 1935-06-14 by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (49 Stat. 375), approved that day, which repealed the Title I provisions delegating power to approve codes and providing for their enforcement. Actor: the Congress (Public Resolution No. 26, 74th Congress). The approval's enforceable operation rested on sections 3(a)-(c) and 10(b) of the Act (held), which is the reason the repeal extinguished it (owner ruling 2026-10-28). Disclosed alternatives: Schechter, May 27, 1935 (earlier; not shown to have extinguished this approval) and EO 7076, June 15, 1935 (later; continues orders only so far as consistent with the amended Act and disclaims code approval and enforcement); see the member checks.

Stay condition terminated by its own terms: the application of the time-and-one-third provision 'shall be stayed until March 1, 1934, at which time such provision shall become effective and have the same force and effect as any other provision of the Code'. Recorded as 1934-03-01, inclusive (the stay runs through the end of that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling; the exclusive reading ends the stay when that day began. Actor: EO 6530 itself. After it ends the provision is a provision of the code, not a command of this order.

research_rationale:
Identity and text (APP page check, jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md, done 2026-10-29): the registered American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved) was read in full. The MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with the same sha256 (d10717868f0e...) has the heading 'Executive Order 6530—Code of Fair Competition for the Medium and Low Priced Jewelry Manufacturing Industry', the date 1933-12-23 (which agrees with the date line of the held text), and a text_sha256 equal to the held file's; the row records the common-crawl WARC location. The 1944 WPA numbered list (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv) carries the same number and date: 'Code of Fair Competition for the Medium and Low Priced Jewelry Manufacturing Industry approved. IV NRA Codes 355. (Dec 23, 1933)'. Quotations are taken from the registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. EO 6530 (December 23, 1933) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Medium and Low Priced Jewelry Manufacturing Industry 'subject to the following condition: That the application of the provision of sub-section (b), Section 1, Article III, which provides for the payment of time and one third for all hours worked by any employee in excess of forty (40) per week, shall be stayed until March 1, 1934, at which time such provision shall become effective and have the same force and effect as any other provision of the Code.' The dossier's single clause (characters 757-1620) holds two commands with different lifetimes, so the inventory is corrected on the registered text into two scopes: the approval sentence (757-1158) and the stay condition (1160-1525); the signature block and Administrator's recommendation that follow are not operative. Stay condition: it ends by its own terms on 1934-03-01, recorded inclusive (the stay runs through that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling; the words 'at which time such provision shall become effective' support the exclusive reading, under which the stay stops when March 1, 1934 begins and the overtime provision applies that day. The dossier's own-terms record (until_event, 1934-03-01) matches. After the stay the overtime provision is a provision of the code, not a command of this order. No held order extends, shortens or revokes the stay (searches below; the type rule's outlier case of a stay later modified by administrative order cannot be excluded beyond the held sources). Approval: First end: 1935-06-14, the day Senate Joint Resolution 113 (Public Resolution No. 26, 74th Congress, 49 Stat. 375, chapter 246) was approved. Section 2 of the resolution reads: 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed', with one proviso that narrows only the section 5 antitrust exemption. It names no code and no order, so it is not a naming instrument (owner ruling 2026-10-21, unnamed instruments), and under the owner's 2026-10-28 ruling a general rule ends a command only where something shows it extinguished that command. What shows it here is the text of the Act under which the order was made (48 Stat. 195, held): section 3(a) is the power to approve a code; section 3(b) makes the provisions of an approved code 'the standards of fair competition for such trade or industry' and a violation an unfair method of competition; section 3(c) gives the district courts jurisdiction to restrain violations of 'any code of fair competition approved under this title'; and section 10(b) lets the President cancel or modify 'any order, approval, license, rule, or regulation issued under this title', which shows the approval was a continuing act that the Act made binding through sections 3(b) and 3(c). The approval commands nothing of its own beyond that statutory operation, and the resolution repealed the approval power and the enforcement of codes together, with no clause preserving approved codes. The order's only operative act, making the code the enforceable standard, therefore ended on 1935-06-14. Alternatives considered and disclosed. (a) Earlier: Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, 295 U.S. 495, decided May 27, 1935 (caption and syllabus held), says at 542 'the code-making authority thus conferred is an unconstitutional delegation of legislative power'. The judgment concerned the Live Poultry Code; it names no other code, and nothing held shows it extinguished this approval on that date (no order of May 27 through June 14 touches any code). If a reviewer holds it ended every approval, the first end would be 1935-05-27; the claim uses June 14 because that is the first date on which held text removes approval and enforcement for all codes. (b) The original expiry of Title I two years after enactment (section 2(c), June 16, 1935) was displaced when the resolution amended section 2(c) to April 1, 1936; it is later than the repeal. (c) Later: EO 7076 (June 15, 1935, held APP text, page record date 1935-06-15; its held transcription omits the signature and date lines) amends all existing Title I executive orders 'so as to continue them in effect and to extend their operation ... until April 1, 1936, so far as consistent with the provisions of the National Industrial Recovery Act as amended and extended', but provides that it 'shall not be construed as an exercise by the President of any authority, or as authorizing any person or agency ... to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition, to provide for the enforcement of such codes'. Because the approval's force came through the provisions the resolution had repealed the day before, continuing it 'so far as consistent' with the Act as amended leaves it no enforceable operation; EO 7076 is therefore recorded here as a disclosed later order and is not treated as an extension or an end. Held EO 7075 (June 15, 1935) likewise refers to the trades 'heretofore subject to codes of fair competition'. (d) A reviewer who reads section 5 as keeping approved codes 'in effect' for antitrust exemption while Title I stood (to April 1, 1936, plus sixty days) could place a later end for that statutory exemption; the exemption is a statutory consequence, not a command of this order, and the resolution's proviso narrowed it to agreements on section 7(a) requirements and on practices already unlawful. That reading would not revive the approval as an enforceable code. Limit: the approved code's own text is not held, so a duration or cancellation term inside it could not be read; no held order, statute, case or index entry shows a code-specific cancellation, amendment, supersession or expiry. Searches run 2026-10-29. (1) A scan of 51,237 txt, jsonl, csv, json and md files under jobs/ (skipping the derivative folders clause-drafts, claim-kit, case-bundles, claim-drafts, x1-class-engine, readiness-tracker and domesday-register, and cache, capture and pdf folders) for the code's title and for citations of this order by number. (2) Every held order text numbered 7060 or higher (APP, Hathi/Commons printed copies, Wikisource, Federal Register, source-ladder) containing the phrase 'codes of fair competition': only EO 7075, EO 7076 and EO 7323 (and an unrelated 1941 board order, EO 9027). (3) The APP index of orders dated 1935-05-15 through 1935-06-25: no order dated 1935-05-27 through 1935-06-14 touches an NRA code; EO 7075 and 7076 (June 15) and EO 7084 and 7085 (June 24, labor boards) are the next NRA orders. (4) The later-events counter-evidence leads file (none for this order). (5) The machine searches current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr (0 hits) and later-events:ofr_catalog (0 hits; its coverage starts in 1937, so it is not relied on alone). Result of (1): hits are only this order's own records and index rows. The phrase 'time and one third' also appears in EO 6393 (Toy and Playthings code) and EO 6450 (Precious Jewelry Producing code), which are other codes and do not mention this order or its stay.

savings.reason: The order states no savings. What survives the repeal is statutory and accrued, not a continuing command of the approval: liabilities and rights that accrued while the code was binding (violations before 1935-06-14, and conduct that complied with it), and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with an approved code 'while this title is in effect ... and for sixty days thereafter' (held, 48 Stat. 195), as narrowed by the resolution's proviso. None of these keeps the approval operative after 1935-06-14. Whether pre-repeal violations remained prosecutable turns on a general saving rule that is not held and is not relied on. For the stay, the overtime provision that took effect on 1934-03-01 is a provision of the code, which ended with the approval's enforceable operation; it is not a surviving command of this order.
